refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement says, “For V^0>0, membership in this cone is exactly the coordinate-speed condition |d\mathbf x/dt|≤c,” but V is a free vector and no curve or coordinate-velocity map is defined. The coordinates x^0=ct alone do not define d\mathbf x/dt for V; the statement needs, for example, the map v(V)=c\mathbf V/V^0.

The Statement defines the reference cone as a subset of R^4 and says it has “boundary speed in (t,\mathbf x) coordinates” c, then compares v_bulk with that cone. It does not define coordinate speed for a vector or null direction. For V^0>0, defining v(V)=c\mathbf V/V^0 would give the comparison an explicit meaning.

The Statement says, “Assume positive C^1 coefficients ζ and τ, set β=τ/ζ,” and then uses ∇_a(βu^a/T), but does not give ζ or τ a domain or codomain. The derivative requires β to be a scalar field on the spacetime domain O; specify, for example, ζ,τ∈C^1(O;(0,∞)).

reader_findings.location: Statement, first paragraph: the coordinate-speed condition |d\mathbf{x}/dt| <= c for V^0 > 0.
reader_findings.evidence: The claim starts from a free vector V=(V^0,\mathbf V) in R^4 but does not define a curve or coordinate-velocity map that makes d\mathbf{x}/dt an object of V. Define v(V)=c\mathbf V/V^0 for V^0>0, then derive from eta(V,V)=-(V^0)^2+|\mathbf V|^2 that eta(V,V)<=0 iff |v(V)|<=c.
